markdown_report:
Select a provenance-backed mutation audit before changing BERT4Rec training. At 10% research progress, verifying that diagnostics exercise the actual pipeline offers a feasible foundation for later ranking improvements.

**Insights from the starting point**

- Electronics has 21.97% negative-outranking on audited training targets. This motivates investigation, but does not establish weak validation HR@10.
- Every audited supervised position contains MASK, yet original-event provenance remains unavailable. Mask presence cannot certify correct target alignment or absence of future-event exposure.
- Live integrity checks leave exported-predictor parity unknown. Training-prefix recovery likewise cannot establish held-out usefulness or explain qualitative skips.

**Insights from related work**

- BERT4Rec replicability research [1] makes masking and inference semantics central to faithful implementation. Actual event-index records can test this contract more directly than item-ID comparisons.
- Recommender metamorphic testing [2] motivates checking predictable relationships between executions. Its existing results do not validate Transformer-specific relations, so each proposed relation needs clean controls.
- Mutation testing [3] motivates evaluating assertions against deliberately introduced faults. Detection measures sensitivity to specified defects; undetected or untested faults remain possible.

These insights define three directions: supervision provenance, deployed-predictor consistency, and diagnostic sensitivity calibration.

| Direction | Existing evidence | Missing evidence | Proposed check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Supervision | MASK-position counts | Source-event alignment | Actual sampler trace replay |
| Deployment | Live score agreement | Saved predictor agreement | Reload identical fixtures |
| Calibration | Structural controls | Fault detection coverage | Isolated mutant matrix |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, with higher difficulty meaning harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Originality: positive / negative | Potential: positive / negative | Difficulty: favorable / challenging |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Actual sampler trace replay [1] | 4/8/4 | Direct pipeline evidence / established tracing | Resolves alignment uncertainty / no demonstrated ranking gain | Local instrumentation / unavailable sampler implementation |
| Exported-predictor parity fixtures [1,2] | 3/8/5 | Connects export to diagnostics / standard parity testing | Detects deployment defects / finite fixture coverage | Reuses scores / requires reload runner |
| Mutant detection matrix [2,3] | 4/7/5 | Family-specific calibration / established mutation testing | Exposes ineffective assertions / artificial fault distribution | Small isolated mutations / clean-control design |

Choose **actual sampler trace replay**, the smallest unresolved integrity step. Record source history indices, selected targets, corruption decisions and retained context for bounded batches. Reconstruct expected inputs from supplied training histories, verifying same-event labels for Cloze examples and strictly earlier context for terminal examples. Repeated target IDs remain legitimate when their event indices differ.

Return measured assertion counts, failures and unavailable reasons through the existing diagnostic adapter; add isolated shifted-label and restored-target controls to calibrate these assertions. Preserve RNG states and the actual training stream. This audit changes neither scoring nor architecture. Keep one checkpoint per category and use only pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 to judge subsequent training revisions; no performance gain is claimed.

idea.description: Instrument the actual corrected BERT4Rec sampler with bounded event-level provenance records, then replay those records against supplied training histories to verify masked-target construction and prefix alignment. Calibrate the assertions with isolated synthetic faults while retaining exactly one independently trained network per category.
idea.motivation: Current diagnostics observe reserved masks but cannot certify the source events, corruption decisions or target alignment that produced them. Resolving this uncertainty is more actionable at 10% progress than attributing qualitative relevance failures to unverified model mechanisms.
idea.implementation_notes: This is a proposed integration, not executable replacement training code: the sampler implementation is not supplied. Add an optional side-channel trace to the actual sampler without changing the loader's (None, sequence, positive, negative) B×L contract. Record user ID, source event indices, branch, crop bounds, original selected labels, corruption choices and supervised positions for a bounded number of batches. Trace recording must consume no extra sampling draws and must not advance a separate training iterator. Replay against public training histories only. Cloze labels must equal original items at their source indices; terminal targets and later events must be absent by event index, while legitimate earlier occurrences remain allowed. Validate the corrected baseline's declared corruption policy rather than assuming all BERT4Rec implementations always replace selected tokens with MASK. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), view.model and all ModelView hooks. Missing trace access returns null with an explicit reason. Restore module modes and RNG states after diagnostic execution. Keep left padding and greatest-nonpadding-position readout, reserved-mask inference, all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per completed epoch. No model or predictor architecture change is required; checkpoint and embedded writer consistency remains mandatory and independently unverified unless a reload runner is available. All host execution consumes the shared budget. Record counts per assertion and fault; synthetic controls do not certify unexercised paths. Do not treat training diagnostics, qualitative feedback or mutant detection as validation accuracy.

originality.positive: Adapts event-level trace replay and fault calibration to the actual BERT4Rec sampler and fixed diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Tracing, replay assertions and mutation testing are established techniques; this is an application rather than a new learning algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Provides auditable supervision evidence that can support controlled sampler and loss experiments across the four datasets.
future_potential.negative: Correct supervision does not guarantee useful recommendations or improved held-out HR@10, and finite traces cannot certify every execution.

code_difficulty.positive: Instrumentation is localized to sampling and diagnostics, with no new network, scorer or inference path.
code_difficulty.negative: Access to the actual sampler is required, and event-index replay, RNG neutrality and faithful trace capture need careful integration.

related_work.title: [1] BERT4Rec replicability study
contributions: Provides implementation and reproducibility context for BERT4Rec's masked-item training and appended-mask prediction.
limitations: Does not certify the supplied sampler, trained checkpoint or exported predictor.
Terminal masking itself is established and should not be presented as a novel contribution.

related_work.title: [2] Recommender metamorphic-testing study (2024)
contributions: Evaluates six metamorphic relations across LibRec, PREA and Surprise, motivating execution-relation checks.
limitations: Its reported scope does not directly validate BERT4Rec masking, padding or event-provenance assertions.

related_work.title: [3] Mutation-testing study on optimisation software (2025)
contributions: Motivates assessing test relations against deliberately faulty implementations and reporting detection sensitivity.
limitations: Transfer to sequential recommendation is proposed rather than demonstrated.
Detection of selected artificial faults does not establish comprehensive pipeline correctness.
